utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I notice that Mr. Dagovic is still in the witness box, and so we will continue with cross-examination. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day. We would agree about some indisputable facts. The first fact is as follows: During your detention at the Samac MUP, you experienced mistreatment and abuse; is this true or not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Fact number two: The chief of police, Stiv Todorovic, and his police officers, practically were responsible during your captivity for everything that was going on; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The question is for everything that's going. That's an improper question, calling for conclusion about all sorts of things. Some of it would be outside the scope of this witness, and I'd object. It's an improper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will narrow the issue, of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fact number three: Members of paramilitary units which were at the Samac MUP carried out certain abuse; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Fact number four: Members of the Serbian police under the command of Stiv Todorovic also abused you; is this right or not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amongst others, yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender into evidence one sketch which was made by this witness. The ERN number is 00182901. It is actually -- depict and description of the MUP area where he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When was it made?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When was it made?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, that's another problem that I want to bring to the attention of this Trial Chamber. In fact, during the preparation of cross-examination of this witness, I noticed that in his statement made on 1994, he speaks about this map and another sketch. And the -- after the verification in checking what was discovered from the OTP to the Defence, I noticed that these two particular documents were not -- were not disclosed, and of course, I made some contacts with my learned friends, and they were so kind to provide us virtually by the end of last week. So it was made -- I assume it was made in 1994. But the ERN numbers are not correspond with the ERN numbers on his previous statement on 1994. So maybe my colleague can clarify that. In the meantime, I would like to tender this into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just want to clarify one thing, Your Honour. We have a signed receipt from this Defence counsel for that statement and the diagrams and it's dated June 9th, 1999. We've had -- several times, the Prosecution has been blamed for not providing the documents. We have a signed receipt. If you want, I can turn it in to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Signed by Mr. Lukicic on his behalf. And we have it signed by all the attorneys. So if there's a problem that one attorney didn't turn them over, that's their type of problem. It shouldn't be blamed on the Prosecution. We've been blamed on several occasions when we have signed receipts for these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I would very much be grateful if I can take a look -- short look on this receipt, because according to my list, I am speaking on behalf of my client, I wasn't able to locate this particular ERN numbers. So if I just have a short look on this receipt, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the usher can assist first with counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because I have all these documents on the CD-ROM, and I have a certain programme when I type, you know, particular ERN number and it doesn't appear. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the usher please show Mr. Pantelic and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, not only is the ERN listed, too, from the documents on the receipt --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I can confirm that these ERN numbers are on this list, but still after the checking of the material discovery of my present client, which is Mr. Blagoje Simic, I don't have these particular ERN numbers in my list. So I kindly ask that this approach from the Prosecutor would be clarified, because as I said, my previous documents were transmitted to the -- to the counsel who is now in charge for this particular crime, Mr. Tadic. But as I said, I don't have on my list of these ERN numbers these particular sketches, so I am not obliged, Your Honours, to have all documents during this case. Contrary, I am obliged when I finish with my client to transmit all relevant documents to the attorney in question. So the OTP is not in possession of the receipt that I signed for my client, Mr. Blagoje Simic, that they gave me these particular sketches. So up to now I don't see -- I don't see this evidence. But we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think so, that we have heard enough explanation, and I'm sure that the Prosecution are satisfied that they did what they could at the time. Perhaps as time goes on, they will make sure that since Mr. Blagoje Simic came on the list much later --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that all the other relevant documents are handed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He came in March 2001, so they were obliged to discover all these materials. Anyhow -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honour please, that raises a considerable problem. I mean, the Prosecution has handed over these documents that are general documents in the case and of a general application to all of these defendants, and this is a clear, clear example, a statement of one witness that applies in many respects to various issues in the case. If the situation is that Mr. Pantelic has lost or given away all the documents that he once received from the Prosecution, then this situation will arise again and again, won't it? So I think that we ought to know, and firmly know, from Mr. Pantelic if indeed he is now missing a large swathe of documents that he once received because he gave them to another counsel. It seems to me that the problem could be solved and not laid at the Prosecution's door by Mr. Pantelic simply saying to counsel, "Can I have a copy of the documents I gave you?" That would, I think, take care of the problem, would it not? If that's not suitable to Mr. Pantelic, then I think a clear indication from him that he is missing a large section of documents be made to us, and that could be done privately, and we will attend to his request. But I wouldn't like this issue to arise again, because of course it would put Mr. Pantelic at a disadvantage if he doesn't have the documents and it puts us at a disadvantage, too. If Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for the explanation, Mr. Di Fazio. I think that is sufficient. I think both parties will make sure that--

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But Your Honour, just to end this, I need to give you few informations. The fact is here as follows: I gave all documents and statement to my colleague, Mr. Lukic. So it is not any more in my possession any page, any document. That is a normal way, how we act. And when I started with Mr. Blagoje Simic, the Prosecutor were obliged to provide me in discovery process with all relevant documents related to my client, Mr. Blagoje Simic. So I mean, it's a little bit of misunderstanding on the part of Prosecution about how these documents were transmitted. So they are in possession of my colleague, Mr. Lukic, and I am not entitled to go into his office and to check up what's going on in his own papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic -- let me ask Mr. Lukic, please. I'm sure you would have no objection to giving copies of all the documents that Mr. Pantelic handed over to you to him. Not that you have an obligation to do so, but as professional etiquette.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. I will do everything to prevent any kind of wrong steps in procedure. But yes, Mr. Pantelic did hand over to me the records and the whole documentation, and of course, I will make sure that I will hand it back to him. But also, I will make available all the material to him handed over to me by the Prosecution. So hopefully that -- the Trial Chamber will permit me to allow access to Mr. Pantelic again to all the documents that he has provided to me and that he can photocopy the documents that he needs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honours. Mr. Usher, could you please give this map to the witness. Sorry, it is on the ELMO. Could I have the ID number or maybe if there is no objection or maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's a sketch, not a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's a sketch. Sorry. That's my mistake. Sketch number -- ERN number 001829 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down for the benefit of the interpreters? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the -- first of all, the interpreters are saying can you slow down, Mr. Pantelic. They are having problems catching up with you. The Prosecution, I'm sure, have got sight of this diagram -- or sketch, rather, alleged to have been drawn by the witness now in the witness box. Is there any objection to having it produced into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It is Exhibit D26/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Usher, I don't think we need your assistance. You can sit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be so kind and tell us whether the markings "SL Samac" stands for Slavonski Samac.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I assume that you sketched this.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Slavonski Samac is on the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This next marking "trees" means that this is the bank towards Croatia and that it's forested; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call it a forest, but yes, there were trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that there were members of Croatian army there, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I wasn't there on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that. Do you have knowledge that there was Croatian army there?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a red marker and on the part of the diagram where it says "SL Samac," could you please write "CRO," which is an abbreviation for "Croatia." Then I would ask you to take the red marker and to mark the garage that you sketched where your relative was killed by a shell.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that's garage number 4, and you marked it with a red cross. You marked garage number 4 with a red cross, the place where your cousin was killed by a shell?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it was his uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, his uncle. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the interpreter -- the interpretation was "cousin."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark, since in your previous testimony you explained what happened at the time of this shelling, could you please indicate with an arrow the direction from which the shell came.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For the record, the witness just made an arrow, which was the direction of the alleged direction of the shelling. Mr. Usher, you can take your seat. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You provided a statement to the Prosecutor's office in 1994; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In my records, it's the 6th and the 7th of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: With your permission, Your Honour, I have a copy on B/C/S version of his statement. So maybe we can place it in front of him, then so we can easily go through certain portions of this statement. It is not my intention to tender it into evidence. It's just a facilitating of communication with the witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in your opinion, the shell was fired by the Serb forces on the Serb town of Samac; is that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am convinced of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But this conviction of yours, do you have any proof of that? Did you discuss this with anybody?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I was at the scene of the crime, I could see certain things for myself. And when I was there after I was released from the camp, I -- after the exchange when I returned to Samac, I had the opportunity to get a better look and even to make a record with a camera of where I was standing, so I filmed or I took pictures of everything. So I assume that my thoughts about it are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood from your previous testimony, while you were questioned by one of my colleagues, you said that one shell fell only. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Into the MUP courtyard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify. Does that mean that there were other shells?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this is what I said on the previous occasion, if you had read that carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that day when the shelling took place, one of the shells fell on the SUP, and the other shells fell on other places on that day.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You heard about the incident at Markale in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What do you know about that incident? Who fired at whom?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is a Bosanski Samac case. As to the firing, as to who fired in Sarajevo at certain times, that's for the Galic trial. That's not a matter for the Bosanski Samac trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my idea is to establish certain, I would say, illogical position of this witness with regard to certain situation. And I'm simply asking about the general knowledge. I wasn't asking, if you will notice, was he work there in Sarajevo. I simply ask whether he knows or not about this event. He said yes. So I have line of questioning where this might be of very much importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But Mr. Pantelic, you are a lawyer, and you know very well that when a witness comes to give evidence, there are limitations as to what he can be asked about. This is a fact witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So on the 28th of October, 1992, when this shelling was carried out, you were in the MUP courtyard; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that the shell came from Croat positions?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm convinced that it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you are not sure.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure, 100 per cent. I can even argument that, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And Mr. Pantelic, the other question -- the other point I've observed is that we've had a lot of questioning about this particular shell which killed his uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: With other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And I'm sure we've had all the explanations the witness has to give and why he thinks it didn't come from Croatia. We've been through that already. I don't think any repetition will do us any good. It's a waste of Court time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's very necessary, because now I am going to tender into evidence another sketch of this witness. The ERN number is 00182899. It's a sketch -- well, I would say a sort of map of town of Samac and neighbouring areas. This sketch was also made by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's Exhibit D27/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If I may ask before Mr. Pantelic cross-examines, if I may ask the Prosecutor. Both D26/1 and D27/1 are sketches made by this witness. Largely -- the writing is in Serbo-Croat; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the Court can ask the registry assistant to ask the Translation Unit to give us the English equivalent of the words by having photocopies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: On 27.1, Your Honour, it's just the names of the towns. So it's nothing that would really need to be translated. On 26/1, there are words like "drvece" and other words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Then it's only 26/1 which requires an English equivalent which the Translation Unit will deal with, on the request of the Court, of course. Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You can proceed with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I understand, you drew this map. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In 1994, when you gave the statement; is that when it was?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but -- I don't know the exact date, but I know that I did draw such a map. I understand this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just could we have a zoom, please, on this map from -- with the assistance of the technical booth, to have, actually, all map on our screen, because there are some neighbouring areas which might be of importance. Could we have more zoom, to have all these page on the screen. No, no. I would prefer to have -- okay. It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I understand this map -- [In English] I would need your assistance. [Interpretation] As far as I understand this map, it's a sketch of Samac, the town of Samac, and the surrounding villages and the area?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it's not a precise map. Compared to the map you used last time, that map was more precise and it was made by experts. This is just a hand-drawn map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is not so important.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for me, it is. Because since Domaljevac, it's not along the river Sava. It's on the Sava. So we moved everything out a little bit towards Obudovac. But everything should actually be a little closer to the river. Just like these Croatian villages that you can see here. Grebnice, Bazik, and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you please wait. Each one of you do pause for the interpreters, otherwise, the record won't make sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be so kind and show us with the pointer in this drawing of yours where the town of Samac is.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this would be the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now, please, indicate for us where the place called Prud is.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there members of HVO in Prud?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I wasn't present, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any members there?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. If there were that many soldiers everywhere around, then they probably would have been able to defend themselves and us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there members of the HVO in Bazic and Domaljevac.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please indicate Bazic and Domaljevac for us?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there members of the HVO there?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard they were there. And when they were exchanged, I saw in Orasje groups that moved around and who told me that they had been present there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, could there be any time limitation? Are we talking prior to the takeover, at the time of the takeover, while he was incarcerated? At what point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because I thought the answer included at the time he was released. So yes, Mr. Pantelic, do particularise the time period to which your questions pertain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The first question was as follows: After April 1992, after 17th of April, 1992, do you know whether in this area that you had just indicated to us, Grebnice, Bazik, Domaljevac, there were any members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After you were exchanged, do you know whether in the region of Domaljevac, Bazic, and Grebnice, there were members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please take a red marker and indicate for us the HVO in this area where you marked Domaljevac, Bazik, Grbnica?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you. I would move this closer to the Sava river a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, all he has is he's heard that there were troops here. Now they're going to have him mark in that area as if he had personally seen the troops there? That's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Within the competence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. If he has seen them, I have no objection. But if it's just he's heard that there were troops there and at some point, that it's not helpful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you see members of the HVO in this area after you were released?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether members of the HVO were present in the area of Bosanski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know even less about that, because it's quite far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information on the presence of the HVO members in the area of Modrica?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know even less about that, because I didn't visit that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the presence of the members of the Muslim army in the Gradacac area?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information concerning the fact that in this area that you indicated here between Samac, Gradacac, and Bazik, there was basically the front line in that area, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were exchanged on what day, please?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was exchanged on the 5th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were exchanged where?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then after that, you went where?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you give any statements to the police in Orasje at that time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you give any statements later on to the police?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I did not. I spent only a short time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that area?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you, but it was a brief period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, how brief?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very brief. I can't tell you exactly. Five, ten days. Perhaps 15 days. Perhaps only two days. This means that upon arriving there, shortly thereafter I went to Croatia to have a medical examination. My medical condition was very poor at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you didn't go back afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After you recovered, you went to one of the Western European countries, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were not a member of the HVO. At least, I suppose you weren't.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that case, it's a lie.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please take a look at page 14 of your 1994 statement. Can you please find in paragraph number 3 of this page, a sentence saying, "All of that took place on the same day on November 5th." It's in the middle of the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please read it for us.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All that took place on the same day on the 5th of November. After I was released" -- "All of that took place on the same day, on November 5th. After my release, I wasn't able to leave Orasje. Instead I had to go back to the Bosnian HVO army."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please stop there. Can you please explain to the Chamber what is the truth? Is it true that you were not a member of the HVO or what you said to the Prosecutor in 1994 is actually true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member of the HVO, and I can explain. The way it's written here means that I wasn't able to go directly to Croatia. It doesn't say here whether I stayed there for three months or two months. And this other thing about the position is not clear to me. I didn't spend a single day at the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you were never at the front.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for a single day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the last paragraph on that page for us.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As I have said, while I was a soldier at the front, I was allowed to go" --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please slow down for us. The paragraph that gives with the following words: "I went back to the front line with the HVO." Please be calm and concentrate.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm very concentrated, unlike you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please read for us.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, when you start reading, read slowly, and please don't be rude to counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I simply wanted to respond in kind. Should I read now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead with what counsel has asked you to read, and read slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I went back to the positions with the HVO. Out of five people that were released from the camp, just like I was, the three of us were sent back to the positions, which is where they probably are today, because they were unable to get papers. When I say "positions," I mean positions or front line between Orasje and Bosanski Samac. The front line is about 2 kilometres away from Bosanski Samac. So this is an absurdity, because this is not the front line of Bosanski Samac, Orasje, because it's 2 kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you don't mind, I simply asked you to read this out calmly for us and not give any comments.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I read on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please wait. I need to check the transcript, because I want to make sure that all the information we need is in there. [In English] You can read after this sentence, which is "The front line is about 2 kilometres away from Bosnia-Herzegovina." So next sentence is as follows -- without any comment, please. Next sentence from your statement, please.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the front line is approximately 2 kilometres from Bosnia-Herzegovina. "Some of the prisoners that were exchanged in Tuzla and fought in Travnik, I'm one of the lucky ones that was able to get out. On Bosanski Samac, Orasje front line I stayed until the 5th of January, 1994, when I was able to arrange for myself to travel. I was in 104th Samac Brigade of the HVO army, as I've said before. While I was a soldier at the front line, I was allowed to go to Croatia and fix my teeth, because my teeth had been pulled out in the camp. I was also arranged to visit my parents. I was given permission to go there. I had a ticket which I was able to pick together with the eight packages, but I wasn't allowed to wear my uniform."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please pause there for us. In 1994 when you gave this statement to the Prosecutor, did you give the statement of your own free will? Did anyone from the Prosecution harass you or give you any kind of promises?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, continue. What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, this was a question.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody harassed me. I gave the statement on my own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You signed this statement, at least the English version of it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So this statement was given two years after the unfortunate events that you experienced in 1992; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So your memory was quite fresh at the time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just as it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain to the Chamber what is the truth in fact. Can you please clarify for us and tell us whether you were a member of the HVO or not.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that I was not, and I can explain. I was in Croatia. I have my refugee papers. I have all the documents that can prove where I was employed and so on. So if you will allow me, I can show this to this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, the problem that we have here is your statement. Did you -- what you just read from your statement in 1994, is this true or not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying for the third time, it is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, why did you lie in 1994, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection to this last statement, characterisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't understand because it seems to be a contradiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He can ask him about the contradiction. He's accusing him of lying. He can say, "Why is it incorrect?" He claims he's got papers. He can ask him why it's incorrect, what's the reason for the contradiction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, perhaps you can ask him -- you've given us two versions now. One version is probably a lie; which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, you've just heard His Honour Judge Singh: One of these versions is a lie. Can you tell us which statement is a lie? Is your statement from 1994 a lie or what you're saying now a lie?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow, I wouldn't call this a lie, because this has been translated many times and I'm not sure in which context it was translated. As I've said, I have papers, I have arguments, I have witnesses who can confirm where I was at the time. This means that I have documents, witnesses. So please go ahead and tell me what do you want me to demonstrate here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps the problem here is that the way the statement which you have just been reading is understood is that you were a member of the HVO and you were even on the front line, as you have read yourself. Now, if you are saying that the translation, or whatever, perhaps the translation was wrong, then you better explain that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for example, I read there in the statement that it said that I considered myself lucky that I was able to leave. And then all of a sudden it says that I was at the front. Perhaps what I originally said was that I considered myself lucky that I didn't have to go to the front. I don't know how it was translated. As I've said, I have papers that I can show to the Chamber. My -- these papers are at home, but if necessary, I can provide them to you tomorrow. And these papers can explain where I was and what I did. It says here that I was at the front line until the 5th of January, 1994, when in fact I arrived in the Netherlands on the 1st of January and I reported on the 14th of January. Which means that there are a lot of things here that don't click together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, we are now talking about the fact whether you were a member of the HVO unit or not. This is the only thing that we are concerned with right now. So what is a lie? Is a part of your statement from 1994 a lie, the part where you say that you were a member of the HVO, or what you are telling the Chamber now is a lie, what you are telling now about yourself not being a member of the HVO? Please tell us what is it.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't call this a lie. I would call this an error. A lie and an error are two different things. So I can explain that this is an error. I don't know how this error came about, perhaps at the time when they were translating it, or if we perhaps remind ourselves under which conditions these statements were given in 1994. So that in itself could lead to an error. And there are other illogical things in this statement. We are here now talking about different things, wood and metal, you know. These are two completely unrelated things, and I don't know how they came to be included in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During your compulsory military service, you served in the engineering corps, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you were expert for mines and explosives, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call myself an expert, but yes, I had some knowledge about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: While you were serving your -- in the military during your compulsory military service, did you work with mines and explosives?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you were arrested in the Samac MUP, did anybody question you about your participation in the armed formations in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Among other things, they questioned me about that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were tried by a military court in Bijeljina, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Based on the criminal report of the police chief of Bosanski Samac, this case was taken over by the military prosecutor; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And after the -- after certain proceedings were launched, the case was suspended; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it took several years.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object. That's not correct. The case was dismissed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't get your --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The case was dismissed, not suspended. Dismissed for no evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You are trying to -- yes. It wasn't correct to say that this -- the case was suspended.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It was dismissed for insufficient evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. That is the position of the Prosecution, as far as the case goes. Yes, Mr. Pantelic. The Prosecution's position is that this case was actually dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you bear with me just a moment, please, I have to consult with my colleagues about these documents so we can clarify that. Although I don't think it's of so big importance whether it was dismissed or suspended, in the particular case. But, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Well, it is not of significant importance whether this case was suspended or dismissed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you don't take issue with the Prosecution's position that it was dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, according to my information, which is not a matter that we can discuss with this particular witness -- according to my information, the case was suspended due to the fact that he was exchanged. That's all. But this witness obviously cannot be informed about this legal fact or a mere -- it's a matter for evidentiary -- one of the submissions, we can raise that in final submission or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't want to waste time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would you allow me a comment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. If the Prosecution think it is important, they will re-examine you. They will ask a question about that, and then you will be allowed to explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sir, in 1992, owing to some family inheritance, you were considered a fairly wealthy man, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call myself a wealthy man, but my father comes from one, yes. But I had a decent life. I had a good standard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was your average salary in March and April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 1500 and 2.000 German marks. And at that time minimum wage was about 460 German Marks. So compared to that, I had a very good earning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you would describe yourself as a reasonable man who has no tendencies to exaggerate.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I can prove that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please turn to page 6 of your 1994 statement. But before you read the relevant paragraph, as far as I remember, you said that in 1992, you drove a Ford Capri.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And it was seized or confiscated by the paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What year was the car made in?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was an '80 something. I don't know exactly what year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How much did it cost at that time in April in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between seven and eight thousand German marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please kindly read the following sentence, in the middle of the second paragraph, which begins with the following words: "Like a true Bosnian."

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As a Bosnia, there was not one evening I would not go out without 1.000 marks in my pocket. I have lost all this because it was stolen from me. And I -- the Serbs -- I have lost all this because it was stolen from me. The Serbs probably killed others for more money. My car cost 73.000 German marks and they took that from me as well."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What you have just read out is not true.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It could be 7.300 German marks. So it could be between seven and eight thousand German marks. So this is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, I've discussed the statement with some of the Defence attorneys. It is illogical in places. It is filled with errors. It is not -- doesn't even follow any order at times. If they -- if you want it as an exhibit, I'll turn it in. He's testified 7300 marks. I think twice he's testified to that. It says 73.000. We've never raised the issue of 73.000. He's trying to be impeached with something that's definitely mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner, if a document is given to the Defence counsel as a statement made by the witness, what do you expect the Defence counsel to do with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Defence counsel actually spoke to me and -- actually, the other counsel had spoken to me and we all had a laugh over it with some of these mistakes, including that one. I just want to notify the Court he's being impeached by errors, by an error on that particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, I hope the Prosecution will do a better job in re-examination and also explain it, because the Defence counsel is supposed to rely on what is given to them as a statement made by the witness. And then if, as it is happening now, that there are some statements which are wrong, then it's up to the witness to explain. And you can do that in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, because -- not to mention this is international criminal court, this is a statement of around 16 pages, which is quite extended statement and very serious, due to the fact that it was made in 1994. And that was my approach, that this is a really important -- probably this statement was one of the, I would say, elements in puzzle for this indictment. So it's obvious it's very important to proceed with this kind of questioning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were also able to describe yourself as a man who was well informed about the events in Samac in 1992 in March and April.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well informed? I don't know what you mean by that. But I was well informed. I knew a lot, in view of the fact that I was working at such a job.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you were curious. You knew a lot of things about your fellow citizens at that time.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't curious, but I noticed some strange doings by my fellow citizens. So this is something that drew my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The atmosphere in Samac was tense, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So Serbs went to Serb restaurants; Muslims went to Muslim restaurants; and Croats went to Croat restaurants; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So all the citizens of Samac, regardless of their ethnicity, went to restaurants and had interactions, socialised. There was no differentiation?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for Cafe AS. Mostly the people of Serb ethnicity went to that cafe, except for members of other ethnicities who happened to be members of the 4th Detachment. I'm talking about the period immediately before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And other cafes which were owned by Croats and Muslims, the guests were of different ethnic groups. They were multi-ethnic.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. I don't know what you mean by that, that they were all Serbs or Muslims or Croats. But there were cafes where all -- members of all three groups went. For example, there was a Muslim-owned cafe which was owned by Adic. So that was frequented mostly by people of Muslim ethnicity. But this doesn't mean that it wasn't also frequented by Serb -- people of Serb ethnicity. The cafe where I worked was multi-ethnic, the place where I worked, the restaurant pizzeria. I don't know whether they were spies or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are a fairly well-informed person. You knew quite well what was going on in the town. We're talking about March and April 1992, as you've said yourself.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I known what was going on, I would have left the town. I didn't know what was going on. I did notice certain things, however, that were being done by my fellow citizens of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Let's look at page 2 of your statement. The last passage before the end, the sentence starts: "I know these things because of the way we talked with each other." Could you please read from that sentence.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I know these things because of the way we talked with each other. For example, we would say -- "

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please go more slowly -- slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "So for example, we would say, "Did you know this woman was having an affair with this man?' I could draw a map and point out every home. I could tell you their names, their date of birth, everything. All these Serb soldiers, I saw at the front. I knew who they were, what kind of cars they had, what kind of clothing they wore. Everyone in Bosanski Samac knows these things."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So you stated this in 1994.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you were involved in the lives of your fellow citizens, who was doing what, these kinds of things. This is something that you were interested in?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This context --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. I haven't asked anything yet. When you asked for asylum, did you provide a statement about the things that happened in Bosanski Samac and the region?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a private matter, and I wouldn't talk about that, and I don't know how you know whether I have been granted asylum or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe, Your Honours, we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can you ask the people responsible for changing the sessions to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To which police did you provide a statement in the period between November 1992 and September 1994, and when precisely?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a statement to the INTERPOL.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that statement, did you mention the events in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, amongst other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you inform the Prosecution about that statement you gave to the INTERPOL?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think that I did. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you gave a statement to the Prosecution in 1994 until today, did you give statements to anybody else in connection with the events in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand exactly from which date when did I give a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you gave a statement to the Prosecution, from September 1994 until now, until today.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not. I don't remember the months exactly, but I gave my first statement in September for the INTERPOL. But I don't know whether I gave a statement to the Prosecution or to the INTERPOL first. But I think I gave a statement to both in the same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to the Prosecution in the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the Prosecution but not to the INTERPOL, not to any other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Orasje in 1992, did you provide a statement to Dragan Lukac, the chief of police?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't remember. I don't think I even saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know Dragan Lukac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I've known him for a very long time, perhaps for 20 years. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw him?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time I saw him was a couple of months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Netherlands, as well as in Bosnia, amongst other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you discussed this case?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We have better things to talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to representatives of the Muslim information agency, AID?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you provide a statement to representatives of the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that there was a Muslim army, but no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My mistake. Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, B and H army.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You're welcome. Re-examination, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'd like to discuss some of the issues that were raised with you on cross-examination. Let's begin with your exchange. There was some discussion of that. Prior to being exchanged in November, did anyone ever ask you whether you wanted to be exchanged at that time, just prior to being exchanged in November of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about two things. Nobody asked me directly. I mean, they asked me, but this wasn't my wish. I was forced to. So I was happy to leave that hell. But basically, I wasn't happy to be leaving my town and my parents, so I was forced. But I had to choose the lesser of two evils.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How old were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And at the time of your exchange, where were the members of your family, your parents, your brother? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My father and I were exchanged on the same day. My mother was exchanged about a month and a half after us, and my brother escaped via Serbia even a year later. So I had to leave my mother and my brother behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Prior to your exchange, were you able to speak to your family and discuss the situation where you were going to be leaving the area?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in view of the fact that I was detained in the camp. I didn't even say goodbye to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where did you want to go at the time of the exchange, if you could have gone somewhere and left the camp?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean when I left the camp, where I wanted to go?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. If you had the opportunity, where did you want to go?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left Bosnia, when I was exchanged, I intended to go. And this wish came true. I wanted to go to a third country.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And were you given any option of where you could go?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No one from Bosanski Samac sat down and discussed the possibility of your exchange with you in November of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There were a number of questions concerning the interrogations. What was your condition during those three interrogations, both physically and emotionally?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in such a state that I was carried on a stretcher. That was the state I was in. I was broken up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But during the interrogations at the SUP, what was your condition?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in a very bad state. I had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When had you been beaten in relation to those interrogations?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would mostly happen before or after the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: During the interrogations, did anyone ask you what happened to you, why you were beaten, why you were in that condition?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have an option whether or not to give a statement during the interrogation, or to even attend an interrogation?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was coerced.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, did anyone ever tell you that you didn't have to speak with us, you can just stay in your cell?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you refuse to give a statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I didn't dare. I was afraid for my life and for the lives of my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you signed three statements and three blanks, blank forms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you asked to sign those statements or ordered to do so, or told to do so?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was ordered, while being beaten. I also have to say that while the -- or as the blank statements were being signed, I was being beaten. And -- but during the interrogation by the police inspectors, I wasn't beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The police officers - let's just get this straight - asked you to sign three statements?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amongst other things. I can't hear -- the army and Serb special forces members were also present, along with the interrogators, the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who had you sign the three blank statements?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was forced by members of the special units who were from Serbia. Amongst others, Laki, Neso, Lugar, Crni.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever inquire why you had to sign any of these six statements?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't dare, since they were very savage. They didn't really look for a reason in order to abuse anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you have refused to sign these statements?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could. But that could have cost me my life. So in other words, I couldn't really refuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were these statements voluntary, these six statements that -- the three blanks that you signed and the three others that you signed for the police inspectors?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing was voluntary in the camp, not even going to the bathroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we look at the two statements? Would the usher please show the witness D28/3, the statement of March -- I'm sorry, May 8th, 1992. Your Honour, do we take the break at quarter of or at 4.00?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We're supposed to take the break at 15.45. We seem to have -- the clock in the courtroom is -- is 15.45. Yes, I think -- I can see that from here. So we shall take our break and continue at 16.15 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Let's go to D28/3 for ID, the statement of May 8th, 1992. Could you read the first line of the section that you said is not true or you did not provide to the police.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime at the end of 1991, my mother, and then the name of my mother, told me that she had registered me in the SDA party. She informed me of this, and I agreed with this. So from then on, what is stated here is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What about the next line: "I did not attend party meetings or pay membership fees"? Did you provide that information?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So from this point here, I didn't say this. What is written here, I did not say. I would not have said something as stupid as that I provided financing for my mother and my father. They had their own earnings, so I was not responsible for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, no. What I -- let's take the sentence, "I did not attend party meetings or pay membership fees." Did you say that to the interrogators?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I said this. But what is stated here underneath, I did not say. So from here -- somewhere from here until the end of the page is something that I did not say at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next paragraph. So the section, "I did not attend party meetings or pay party membership fees," just that sentence, just that sentence alone, do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I did. As I said but not in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Just one sentence at a time. The next paragraph. I will read it, and you tell me whether or not you said it: "I do not remember the exact date, but it must have been about two months ago, when Ratif Atic, also known as Rajec, stopped me in the street and told me to come to his cafe when I had time. I went to see him two or three days later and he asked me whether I would like join a newly established SDA unit and be issued a weapon. I told him that I worked as a waiter to support my parents and that I did not have the time for such nonsense. I did not show any interest later and was never called again." That paragraph which was read to you, did you say that to the interrogators on or about May 8th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let us continue, that same paragraph. My next question is: Is that true? Did those things happen relating to Ratif Atic which are listed in this statement, that statement I just read to you, did that happen? Not whether or not you were asked; did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see the man, and he didn't ask me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let us look at the next paragraph. I will read it. "About 20 days ago when the news broke about the formation of the TO (Territorial Defence) in Bosanski Samac, a man nicknamed Ibela stopped me in the street and asked me if I wanted to join the TO in Bosanski Samac. He said that the unit would consist of Serbs, Croats, and Muslims. I accepted his offer without hesitation, and I even told him that my brother, Safet Dagovic, would join too, although I had not consulted him first." Did you provide that information to the interrogators on or about May 8th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Next question: That paragraph which you claim you did not provide, is that information true or false?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: False.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So it never happened.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now look at the next statement, D29/3 for ID. Did you get a chance to read it? What is the last line of the information that you provided? Could you please read that last line.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will read the last sentence. "I also would like to state that I did not participate in any way in the formation of the SDA."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. The next sentence, let me read the remaining part of that paragraph. "I agreed to join the BH TO two or three days before the war broke out in our municipality because Muhamed Bicic, also known as Beca, asked me to join and explained to me that the unit would consist of Serb, Croats, and Muslims and that Zoran Blagojevic would be a commander of the Bosanski Samac unit. However, when I realised who the members were, I did not take any part of it. I was told that my name was on the list of volunteers for the defence of the town, but I cannot explain how it got there." Did you provide that information to the police interrogators?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is the information concerning Muhamed Bicic and Ibrahim Salkic true, or did that in fact happen? Did it happen, or did it not happen?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Last week, during cross-examination by Mr. Zecevic, a question arose concerning your arrest. And two of the Judges, Judge Singh and Judge Williams, asked you questions concerning your arrest, and we never had an answer. Our question to you, based on the Court's question, is: Why were you arrested, if you know, on or about May 5, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did any of the police officers, soldiers, ever tell you why you were being arrested?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They never told me directly why. The only reason was that I differed from them, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you say you differed from them, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't of the same ethnicity as them, and I also wasn't a member of the 4th Detachment or any other paramilitary formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was your arrest the result of any criminal misconduct on your part?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your fellow citizens who were held with you at the SUP, at the police station, were those persons members -- were those persons members of the military, or were they civilians?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Of what ethnic group were all these people that were being held at the SUP?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who were held in the SUP were Bosniaks, Muslims, or Croats, Catholics.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why were they arrested, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose for the same reason as I was, which means that they were of a different ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why were those persons beaten, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see a reason to beat them, but they were beaten. They beat us, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And why were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the persons who held you and beat you, of what ethnic group were they?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Serbs, Orthodox.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, there was some talk concerning the vehicle which you owned. Could you please describe that vehicle to this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That vehicle was Ford Capri. As I've stated before, it was some ten years old at the time. The price I paid for that car was between 7 and 8 thousand German marks, so it wasn't 73.000 marks, as was written in the statements. I don't know of any Ford vehicle costing that much. What I said I stated clearly, everybody knows what car I drove at the time, so I couldn't have said anything that wasn't true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, what condition was the car in, in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in good condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what happened to it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My car was driven by a member of the 4th Detachment. I named that man last time, but I can repeat here that his name is Markovic, Nino. He was the son of Borivoje, known as Smudj. I saw him drive my car. And it was in a very bad condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ask for your permission to take the car, or did anyone pay you for the car?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was all done while they beat me, which means that the car was forcibly confiscated from me, together with the car's papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, there was some talk concerning forced labour during cross-examination. And there was an indication that your brother worked a certain number of days. Was your brother ever paid for any of the work which he performed?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you ever paid for any of the work which you performed?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were your parents ever paid for any of the work which they were forced to perform?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let us move on. You were released or exchanged in November of 1992. Could you please tell us what you did from November through the end of -- from November 1992 through the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the exchange, I went to Orasje. After a certain time, but brief amount of time, which means just a few days, I went to Croatia. In Croatia, I started working in Istria to be precise, in Novi Grad. I worked there as a waiter, and I can say with certainty when it comes to these dates and my alleged serving in the HVO, I can tell you that I can show you a document which shows that I was, on the 8th of December, in Croatia. And it's not true that I left Croatia on the -- for the first time on the 5th of January, 1994, because I, in fact, arrived in the Netherlands on the 1st of January. So that is not true. If you will allow me, I can show you the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you have it with you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He has ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What document is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document that was issued to me by the International Red Cross in Zagreb on the 8th of December, 1992, which means that it was issued to me personally. And that was a few days after I was exchanged, perhaps a month after I was exchanged. This is the document I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, maybe you should look at it --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- and see whether or not we should proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can show it to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
